fields: A company must centrally collect resource logs from hundreds of Azure resources and analyse them with KQL, alerts and workbooks. Which Azure Monitor log store should you recommend?
A Log Analytics workspace, fed by a diagnostic setting on each resource. A storage account is cheaper but can't run KQL or alerts.
A security team runs a third-party SIEM such as Splunk and needs Azure resource logs streamed to it in near real time. Which diagnostic settings destination should you recommend?
Azure Event Hubs: the SIEM reads the stream from the event hub. Storage is a batch archive and Log Analytics is an Azure-native query store.
Logs already land in a Log Analytics workspace and must also flow continuously to an event hub. Which Log Analytics feature does this?
Data export rules, which stream chosen workspace tables to a storage account or event hub as data arrives.
An Azure Monitor diagnostic setting can send to a {{c1::Log Analytics workspace}}, a {{c2::storage account}}, an {{c3::event hub}} or an {{c4::Azure Monitor partner solution}}.
Each destination type can be used once per setting.
Azure audit logs must be kept for 7 years, tamper-proof, at the lowest cost, and are rarely queried. What should you recommend?
Route them with diagnostic settings to an Azure Storage account with an immutability (WORM) policy and lifecycle tiering to cool, cold or archive.
Log Analytics long-term retention or immutable blob storage: which suits 7-year audit logs that still need occasional KQL access?
Log Analytics long-term retention, read through search jobs or restore. Immutable blob storage is cheaper and tamper-proof but has no KQL.
What is the default retention for Analytics tables in an Azure Log Analytics workspace?
30 days, or 90 days for Microsoft Sentinel and Application Insights tables.
A team ingests high-volume verbose logs into Log Analytics that are used only for occasional troubleshooting, never for alerts. How can you cut the cost?
Move those tables to a cheaper table plan (Basic or Auxiliary) instead of Analytics. They give up full KQL and alerting, which this data doesn't need.
Log Analytics Basic or Analytics table plan: which supports alert rules and full KQL?
Analytics. Basic has cheaper ingestion but limited KQL and a per-query charge, so it suits verbose troubleshooting logs.
A workspace ingests a steady 200 GB of logs per day. How can you lower the Log Analytics price per GB?
Buy a commitment tier (they start at 100 GB/day), which discounts ingestion compared with pay-as-you-go.
You need Windows event logs, Syslog and performance counters from Azure VMs and on-premises servers in Log Analytics. What should you recommend?
The Azure Monitor Agent configured by data collection rules; onboard the on-premises servers with Azure Arc first.
Why don't Azure diagnostic settings capture Windows event logs or Syslog from a VM?
They export platform and resource logs from the Azure fabric. Guest OS logs need an agent inside the VM: the Azure Monitor Agent.
Before log data is stored in Log Analytics, you must drop a column of personal data and filter out low-value records to cut cost. Which feature should you use?
DCR transformations: KQL applied at ingestion, so the dropped data is never stored or billed. Filtering at query time saves nothing.
How long does Azure keep Activity log events by default?
90 days. The Activity log records control-plane operations, such as who deleted a resource.
A company needs a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR to detect threats across Azure, Microsoft 365 and on-premises, with automated response. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Sentinel on a Log Analytics workspace, with data connectors, analytics rules and Logic Apps playbooks.
Microsoft Sentinel or Microsoft Defender for Cloud: which one is the SIEM?
Sentinel. Defender for Cloud handles posture and workload protection, and its alerts can flow into Sentinel.
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and audit logs must go to Log Analytics for long-term analysis and alerting. What do you configure?
A diagnostic setting in Microsoft Entra ID that targets the workspace.
When should an Azure Monitor design use more than one Log Analytics workspace?
Only for a hard need: data sovereignty, separate billing or ownership, a different tenant, or strict access isolation. Otherwise start with one central workspace.
App owners must see logs only for resources they can access in Azure RBAC, while all data sits in one shared Log Analytics workspace. What should you configure?
Access control mode Use resource or workspace permissions (resource-context access). Table-level RBAC can narrow it further.
Developers need request rates, response times, failures, dependency tracking and distributed tracing for an App Service web app. What should you recommend?
Workspace-based Application Insights, instrumented with the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry distro or auto-instrumentation.
VM insights or Application Insights: which shows code-level request and dependency telemetry?
Application Insights. VM insights watches the infrastructure: guest performance and process maps.
A public website must be checked for reachability from several geographic locations, with an alert when it fails. Which Azure Monitor feature should you recommend?
Application Insights standard availability tests with an alert rule. Connection Monitor tests network paths between endpoints you control.
Operations wants performance trends for all Azure VMs plus a map of processes and network dependencies between servers. What should you recommend?
VM insights. Its Map feature needs the Dependency agent alongside the Azure Monitor Agent.
An AKS team wants Prometheus metrics without running a Prometheus server, and Grafana dashboards without managing Grafana. What should you recommend?
Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus plus Azure Managed Grafana, with Container insights for container logs.
A VM can't reach a remote endpoint and you suspect an NSG rule. Which Network Watcher tool shows whether the traffic is allowed and which rule decides it?
IP flow verify: it tests the 5-tuple and names the NSG rule that allows or denies it.
You need continuous monitoring of latency, packet loss and reachability between Azure VMs and on-premises servers over ExpressRoute or VPN, with alerts. What should you recommend?
Network Watcher Connection Monitor. IP flow verify and connection troubleshoot are one-off checks, not continuous monitoring.
Security wants to see which IPs and ports talk to workloads in an Azure virtual network, spot traffic hot spots and detect unusual flows. What should you recommend?
Virtual network flow logs sent to storage, analysed with Traffic analytics in a Log Analytics workspace.
Azure Monitor: when do you choose a log search alert over a metric alert?
When the condition needs a KQL query over log data, such as joins or complex filters. Metric alerts suit near-real-time numeric thresholds.
Which Azure Monitor alert type fires when a resource is deleted or a Service Health event occurs?
An activity log alert, which watches control-plane events plus Service Health and Resource Health.
Several Azure Monitor alert rules must email on-call, send an SMS, open an ITSM ticket and trigger a Logic App. How do you design this with minimal duplication?
One reusable action group with those actions, attached to every alert rule.
Notifications from all Azure Monitor alerts in a subscription must be muted during a weekly maintenance window, without editing each rule. What should you use?
An alert processing rule with a suppression action on a recurring schedule, scoped to the subscription.
You must be notified when an Azure outage, planned maintenance or health advisory affects the services and regions you use. What should you configure?
Service Health alerts: an activity log alert on Service Health events, with an action group.
Azure Service Health or Resource Health: which tells you that one specific VM is unavailable?
Resource Health. Service Health reports service- or region-wide incidents that affect your subscriptions.
Azure Workbooks or portal dashboards: which suits rich, interactive troubleshooting reports over monitoring data?
Azure Workbooks, which mix text, KQL, metrics and parameters. Dashboards are simple pinned tiles.
Defender for Cloud alerts and recommendations must be kept longer than the portal keeps them and correlated in a SIEM. What should you configure?
Continuous export in Defender for Cloud, to a Log Analytics workspace or to Event Hubs for a third-party SIEM.
A metric such as requests per second has strong daily and weekly seasonality, so static thresholds cause false Azure Monitor alerts. What should you use?
A metric alert with dynamic thresholds, which learn the seasonal baseline.
Thousands of resources across many subscriptions, including future ones, must automatically get diagnostic settings that send logs to a central workspace. What should you recommend?
Azure Policy deployIfNotExists definitions (the built-in diagnostic-setting initiatives) assigned at a management group, plus remediation tasks for existing resources.
You need to query the current configuration of resources across all subscriptions quickly, for example every VM missing a tag. Which Azure service should you use?
Azure Resource Graph: KQL over resource properties across subscriptions and management groups. Log Analytics holds telemetry, not the inventory.
A company syncs on-premises AD to Microsoft Entra ID and wants the simplest hybrid sign-in with the least on-premises infrastructure, plus leaked-credential detection. Which method?
Password hash synchronization with Seamless SSO: sign-in doesn't depend on on-premises servers, and it enables leaked-credential detection.
Why enable password hash sync as a backup even when Microsoft Entra ID uses pass-through authentication?
If on-premises AD or the PTA agents fail, you can switch sign-in to PHS and keep cloud sign-in working. It also enables leaked-credential detection.
Policy forbids password hashes in the cloud and requires on-premises AD account rules such as logon hours at sign-in, without AD FS. Which Microsoft Entra sign-in method?
Pass-through authentication: on-premises agents validate passwords against AD, so hashes stay on-premises and AD policies apply.
When is federation (AD FS or a third-party IdP) the right Microsoft Entra hybrid sign-in choice?
Only when cloud authentication can't meet a requirement, such as a third-party IdP that must stay authoritative. Otherwise prefer PHS or PTA.

After an acquisition, users from several disconnected AD forests with no trust or connectivity must sync to one Microsoft Entra tenant with lightweight, highly available agents. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync: lightweight provisioning agents, configuration held in the cloud, and support for disconnected forests.
Entra Cloud Sync or Entra Connect Sync: which do you need for cross-forest attribute merging and advanced sync rules?
Entra Connect Sync. Cloud Sync is lighter and handles disconnected forests, but lacks those advanced features.
Users must use MFA only when signing in from outside the corporate network or from non-compliant devices. Which Microsoft Entra feature should you recommend?
A Conditional Access policy using named locations and device compliance, with a require-MFA grant. Security defaults can't be scoped this way.
MFA must be required automatically for risky sign-ins, and users with leaked credentials must change their password. Which Microsoft Entra capability is needed?
Entra ID Protection with risk-based Conditional Access (sign-in risk and user risk). It requires Entra ID P2.
Why do hybrid users need password hash sync for Microsoft Entra leaked-credential detection?
ID Protection matches leaked credentials against the password hashes held in Entra ID; without PHS it has nothing to compare.
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2: which licence adds PIM and risk-based Conditional Access?
P2. P1 covers Conditional Access, dynamic groups, SSPR writeback and application proxy.
Administrators must use phishing-resistant, passwordless Microsoft Entra sign-in. Which methods qualify?
FIDO2 security keys or passkeys, Windows Hello for Business, and certificate-based authentication.
How do you enforce phishing-resistant MFA for admins with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access?
Require the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength. SMS, voice and push approvals don't satisfy it.
A new consumer web app needs self-service sign-up, Google and Facebook logins and branded sign-in pages. Which Microsoft identity service should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra External ID in an external tenant (CIAM).
Partner employees must reach your internal apps and SharePoint with their own corporate credentials, and you won't manage their passwords. Which Microsoft Entra feature?
Entra External ID B2B collaboration: invite them as guest users who sign in with their home credentials.
Entra B2B collaboration or B2B direct connect: which gives Teams shared-channel access without a guest object?
B2B direct connect. B2B collaboration creates a guest user in your tenant.
Guests from a partner tenant should not be prompted again for MFA they already did at home. What do you configure in Microsoft Entra ID?
Cross-tenant access settings (inbound trust): trust MFA, and optionally compliant-device claims, from the partner tenant.
Employees must sign in once to a third-party SAML SaaS app and be provisioned and deprovisioned there automatically. What should you recommend in Microsoft Entra ID?
An enterprise application with SAML SSO and automatic SCIM provisioning.
A lift-and-shift app in Azure needs LDAP, NTLM, Kerberos and Group Policy, but nobody wants to run domain controllers. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra Domain Services: a managed domain synced from Entra ID.
Entra Domain Services or AD DS on Azure VMs: which do you need for schema extensions and full domain admin control?
AD DS domain controllers on Azure VMs. Entra Domain Services is managed, so it gives no Domain Admin rights or schema changes.
An App Service app must read Key Vault secrets and connect to Azure SQL without credentials in code or config. What should you recommend?
A managed identity on the app, granted Key Vault Secrets User and an Entra-authenticated database user in Azure SQL.
Azure managed identities: when do you choose user-assigned over system-assigned?
When the identity must be shared by several resources, pre-authorised before deployment, or survive resources being recreated.
A GitHub Actions pipeline outside Azure must deploy to Azure without storing any long-lived secret. What should you recommend?
Workload identity federation: a federated credential on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity that trusts GitHub's OIDC tokens.
Azure RBAC roles or Microsoft Entra roles: which control access to users, groups and tenant settings?
Microsoft Entra roles, such as User Administrator. Azure RBAC roles such as Contributor govern Azure resources.
How can a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator regain access to every Azure subscription in the tenant?
By elevating access, which grants User Access Administrator at root scope (/). Use it only for recovery, then remove it.
Azure RBAC Owner or Contributor: what can Owner do that Contributor can't?
Assign roles to others. Both can fully manage resources.
A team lead may grant only Storage Blob Data Reader to others in a resource group, nothing more privileged. What should you recommend in Azure RBAC?
Role Based Access Control Administrator with a delegation condition limiting assignable roles. Owner or User Access Administrator could grant anything.
At which scopes can an Azure RBAC role be assigned?
Management group, subscription, resource group and resource, from broadest to narrowest.
Can you create Azure deny assignments yourself?
No. Azure creates them, for example from deployment stack deny settings or managed applications.
An Azure role assignment allows an action that a deny assignment blocks. Which wins?
The deny assignment; it takes precedence over role assignments.
Operators must start, restart and read Azure VMs but not create or delete them, and no built-in role fits. What should you recommend?
A custom Azure role with only the VM read, start and restart actions and suitable assignable scopes. Virtual Machine Contributor grants too much.
Users should read only blobs whose project index tag matches their own project attribute, without one role assignment per container. What should you recommend?
Azure ABAC: a role assignment condition on Storage Blob Data Reader that compares blob index tags with principal attributes.
Admins must have no standing Owner access: they request it just-in-time with approval, justification and MFA, and lose it after a few hours. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management with eligible assignments and time-bound activation.
How should you protect a Microsoft Entra tenant against lockout if MFA, Conditional Access or federation fails?
Keep at least two cloud-only emergency access accounts with permanent Global Administrator, strong credentials, and alerts on every sign-in.
Remote users need an on-premises IIS app using Integrated Windows Authentication, with Entra pre-authentication, MFA and SSO, no VPN and no inbound ports. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra application proxy with an on-premises private network connector, using Kerberos constrained delegation for SSO.
Why does Microsoft Entra application proxy need no inbound firewall ports?
Its on-premises private network connector makes only outbound connections to the cloud service.
Remote users need Zero Trust access to on-premises non-web resources such as RDP, SSH, SMB and SQL, with per-app Conditional Access, replacing the VPN. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Entra Private Access, part of Global Secure Access, using its client and private network connectors.
Entra application proxy or Entra Private Access: which can publish RDP, SSH or SMB?
Private Access, which handles any TCP or UDP app. Application proxy publishes only HTTP and HTTPS web apps.
Azure Key Vault Standard or Premium: which offers HSM-protected keys?
Premium, on FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. Standard keys are software-protected (FIPS 140-2 Level 1).
Can Azure Key Vault Managed HSM store secrets and certificates?
No, only keys. Secrets and certificates belong in a Standard or Premium vault.
Customer-managed keys must sit in a single-tenant FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSM where the customer, not Microsoft, holds the root of trust. What should you recommend?
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. Premium also uses Level 3 HSMs, but it is multitenant with a Microsoft-held root of trust.
Azure Key Vault permission model: RBAC or vault access policies, which should you recommend?
Azure RBAC: it works with PIM, can scope down to a single secret or key, and separates management from data access.
Why are Azure Key Vault access policies a privilege-escalation risk?
Anyone with write access to the vault, such as Key Vault Contributor, can add an access policy granting themselves data access.
What is the retention range for Azure Key Vault soft delete?
7 to 90 days (default 90), fixed when the vault is created. Soft delete itself can't be turned off.
What must an Azure Key Vault have enabled before Azure Storage or SQL TDE can use its customer-managed keys?
Soft delete and purge protection.
A customer-managed key in Azure Key Vault must rotate every 90 days automatically, and dependent services must pick up the new version without code changes. What should you recommend?
A key rotation policy (autorotation), with services referencing the key by a versionless key URI.
How do you automate rotation of a password stored as an Azure Key Vault secret?
Handle the Event Grid near-expiry event with an Azure Function that rotates the secret.
Apps read settings from Azure App Configuration, but some values are secrets. Where should those secrets be stored?
In Key Vault, referenced from App Configuration with a Key Vault reference, never as plain configuration values.
How can an App Service or Functions app consume a Key Vault secret as an app setting without code changes?
A Key Vault reference in the setting (@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=...)), with the app's managed identity granted Key Vault Secrets User.
Azure Key Vault topology: one shared vault for everything, or several vaults?
One vault per application, per environment, per region. It limits blast radius and keeps throttling limits separate.
Azure Key Vault must be reachable only from your virtual networks, never over the public internet. What should you recommend?
A private endpoint (privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net DNS zone) with public network access disabled. Firewall rules alone keep the public endpoint.
Which Microsoft Entra feature updates group membership automatically from user attributes such as department?
Dynamic membership groups.
Hybrid users must reset forgotten passwords in the cloud and have the new password written back to on-premises AD. What do you need in Microsoft Entra ID?
SSPR with password writeback, through Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync. It requires Entra ID P1.
How many Azure management groups can one Microsoft Entra tenant hold?
A policy restricting allowed regions must cover all current and future subscriptions, and subscription owners must not override it. Where should you assign the Azure Policy?
At a management group above all subscriptions. Child scopes inherit it, and subscription owners can't change a parent assignment.
New Azure subscriptions land under the tenant root group and escape governance. What should you configure?
A default management group for new subscriptions, such as Sandbox, in management group hierarchy settings.
CAF guidance: should you create separate Azure management groups for production, test and development?
No. Separate environments by subscription under the same workload management group; use management groups for policy archetypes such as Corp and Online.
In the Azure landing zone management group hierarchy, which groups sit under the intermediate root?
Platform, Landing zones (Corp and Online), Sandbox and Decommissioned.
Azure landing zones: Corp or Online management group for an internet-facing app?
Online. Corp is for workloads connected privately to the hub network.
In Azure landing zones, how are new application subscriptions created consistently?
Through subscription vending: an automated process that provisions a governed subscription into the right management group.
When should an Azure design use a separate subscription rather than another resource group?
When you need a separate billing, quota, or access and policy boundary. Resource groups only group resources that share a lifecycle.
How many resource groups can one Azure subscription hold?
Are tags on an Azure resource group inherited by the resources inside it?
No, not by default.
Resources must carry the CostCenter tag of their resource group. Which Azure Policy approach should you recommend?
The built-in Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing policy (modify effect), plus a remediation task for existing resources.
Finance needs costs grouped by department, but many resources are untagged; subscriptions and resource groups do carry tags. What's the least-effort Azure cost reporting fix?
Turn on tag inheritance in Cost Management: subscription and resource group tags are applied to usage records, not to the resources.
Every new resource group must have Owner and CostCenter tags, and creation must fail without them. Which Azure Policy effect?
deny, for example the built-in Require a tag on resource groups. audit would only flag it; modify would add a default value.
Azure Policy audit or deny: what does each do to a non-compliant request?
deny blocks the create or update; audit lets it through and records non-compliance.
Azure Policy {{c1::modify}} changes tags or properties on the resource itself, while {{c2::deployIfNotExists}} deploys a missing related resource.
Every Azure VM must have the Azure Monitor Agent extension, installed automatically if missing. Which Azure Policy effect?
deployIfNotExists, with a managed identity on the assignment and a remediation task for existing VMs.
Databases tagged env=prod must not be deletable by anyone, but configuration changes must still work. Which Azure Policy effect?
denyAction on the delete action, the only action it can block. Other changes go through.
You assigned an Azure Policy with modify or deployIfNotExists, but existing resources stay non-compliant. Why?
Those effects act only on new or updated resources. Run a remediation task; the assignment's managed identity needs the required roles.
You must apply 40 related Azure Policies, such as ISO 27001 controls, as one unit with one compliance score and shared parameters. What should you use?
An initiative (policy set definition), usually assigned at a management group.
You want to see the impact of a new Azure Policy deny on existing resources before blocking anything. What should you do?
Assign it with enforcement mode DoNotEnforce: compliance is evaluated and reported, but nothing is blocked.
One resource group needs a temporary, documented exception from an Azure Policy assigned at a management group. What should you use?
A policy exemption (Waiver or Mitigated) with an expiration date. Exclusions (notScopes) are permanent and carry no documentation.
Auditors want a dashboard showing how Azure resources meet PCI DSS and ISO 27001 controls. What should you recommend?
The Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard, with those standards added.
You must audit settings inside the guest OS, such as password policy, on Azure VMs and Arc-enabled servers. What should you recommend?
Azure Machine Configuration (formerly Guest Configuration) policies. Ordinary Azure Policy sees only ARM properties.
Azure resource locks: CanNotDelete or ReadOnly, which still allows changes?
CanNotDelete: read and modify are allowed, only delete is blocked. ReadOnly blocks every update.
Why can a ReadOnly lock on a storage account break tools that only read data?
Listing storage account keys is a POST operation, which ReadOnly blocks, so key-based access fails.
Azure Blueprints is retiring. What should you recommend for deploying a repeatable environment with role and policy assignments as one unit, protected against changes?
Azure Deployment Stacks with deny settings, keeping versioned templates as template specs or in Git.
How do Azure deployment stack deny settings protect the stack's resources?
They create deny assignments (denyDelete or denyWriteAndDelete) on the managed resources.
Azure template specs or deployment stacks: which only stores and versions templates?
Template specs: versioned ARM or Bicep templates shared via RBAC. Deployment stacks deploy and manage resources as a unit.
Managers must be alerted at 80% and 100% of a monthly amount, and a runbook must shut down dev VMs at the threshold. Which Azure Cost Management feature?
A budget with those thresholds, tied to an action group that runs the runbook.
Does an Azure Cost Management budget stop spending when it is exceeded?
No. Budgets only alert or trigger actions; any shutdown must be automated by you.
Guest access to groups and apps must be re-certified quarterly, with access removed if reviewers deny or don't respond. Which Microsoft Entra feature?
Recurring access reviews with auto-apply and if reviewers don't respond: remove access.
Partner users must request a bundle of a Teams group, a SharePoint site and an app, with sponsor approval, 90-day expiry and guests created on approval. Which Microsoft Entra feature?
Entitlement management: an access package whose policy targets the partner as a connected organization, with approval and expiry.
HR-driven joiner and leaver tasks, such as issuing a Temporary Access Pass before day one and removing licences on the last day, must run automatically. Which Microsoft Entra feature?
Lifecycle workflows, which need Microsoft Entra ID Governance licensing; P2 alone isn't enough.
Users must accept a legal disclaimer before using specific apps, with acceptance tracked. Which Microsoft Entra feature?
Terms of use, enforced as a Conditional Access grant control. It needs Entra ID P1.
Privileged access must be reviewed regularly so unused eligible or active Azure Owner assignments are removed. Which Microsoft Entra features should you combine?
PIM for the Azure roles plus recurring access reviews of those PIM role assignments.
A company is migrating a SQL Server app that relies on SQL Server Agent jobs, cross-database queries, CLR and Service Broker. They want PaaS with minimal code changes. What should you recommend?
Azure SQL Managed Instance — near-full engine compatibility, including instance-scoped features. SQL Database lacks them; SQL on a VM works but is IaaS.
Azure SQL Database or SQL Managed Instance: which supports SQL Server Agent and native cross-database queries?
SQL Managed Instance. SQL Database has no SQL Agent (use elastic jobs) and only elastic query for cross-database work.
When should you choose SQL Server on Azure VMs over Azure SQL Managed Instance?
When you need OS-level access or full control of the instance — for example SSRS/SSAS on the same server, FILESTREAM, or third-party agents. You then own OS and SQL patching.
A new cloud-native app needs one relational database with the least administrative effort and built-in HA, and uses no instance-level SQL Server features. Which Azure service fits best?
Azure SQL Database (single database) — patching, backups and HA are built in. SQL MI costs more and is meant for lift-and-shift needing instance features.
In Azure SQL Database, what replaces SQL Server Agent for scheduling T-SQL jobs across many databases?
Elastic jobs. SQL Agent exists only in SQL Managed Instance and SQL Server on VMs.
A company runs PostgreSQL apps and wants a managed Azure service with zone-redundant HA, stop/start to save cost, and control over maintenance windows. What should you recommend?
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Single Server is retired.
A new PostgreSQL workload on Azure needs horizontal scale-out (sharding with Citus). What should you recommend?
Elastic clusters in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path and not recommended for new projects.
A team moves a LAMP app's MySQL database to Azure PaaS, needing zone-redundant HA in production and a low-cost burstable tier for dev/test. What should you recommend?
Azure Database for MySQL flexible server — Burstable tier for dev/test, zone-redundant HA for production. Single Server is retired.
Azure SQL Database DTU or vCore: which purchasing model lets you choose compute and storage independently?
vCore. DTU bundles compute, storage and I/O into one measure — simpler, but less flexible.
Azure SQL Database service tiers: the DTU model offers {{c1::Basic, Standard and Premium}}; the vCore model offers {{c2::General Purpose, Business Critical and Hyperscale}}.
Which Azure SQL Database purchasing model is required for Hyperscale and the serverless compute tier?
vCore. Neither Hyperscale nor serverless exists in the DTU model.
A company has SQL Server licenses with Software Assurance and wants to minimise Azure SQL Database cost. Which pricing option should you use?
The vCore model with Azure Hybrid Benefit, plus reserved capacity. DTU prices include the license, so the benefit can't apply.

Azure SQL Database vCore tiers: {{c1::General Purpose}} is budget-oriented on remote storage; {{c2::Business Critical}} runs on local SSD with several replicas, one readable for free; {{c3::Hyperscale}} uses distributed storage up to 128 TB with fast scaling and snapshot backups.
An OLTP app needs the lowest I/O latency, the highest resilience to failures, and a read-only replica at no extra cost for reporting. Which Azure SQL Database tier?
Business Critical (vCore; Premium in DTU terms). General Purpose uses remote storage and has no free readable replica.
What is the maximum size of a single Azure SQL Database Hyperscale database?
128 TB. A database inside a Hyperscale elastic pool can reach 100 TB.
A single Azure SQL database will grow to 60 TB and needs fast backups and restores regardless of size, plus quick compute scaling. Which tier?
Hyperscale. General Purpose and Business Critical top out at a few TB.
How many HA secondary replicas can an Azure SQL Database Hyperscale database have?
0 to 4. They are hot standbys, readable, and always the same compute size as the primary.
Several reporting teams need heavy read-only queries on a Hyperscale database, each with different compute sizes and separate logins, without affecting the primary. What should you use?
Hyperscale named replicas, one per workload. HA replicas always match the primary's size; named replicas size independently and can sit on another logical server.
A dev/test Azure SQL database is used intermittently, sits idle for hours, and the company wants to pay nothing for compute while idle. What should you recommend?
The serverless compute tier with auto-pause enabled. While paused you pay only for storage.
Why does an app using Azure SQL Database serverless with auto-pause need connection retry logic?
The first login resumes the paused database, and that connection can fail with a transient error (40613) until the resume completes.

An Azure SQL Database serverless database never auto-pauses while it uses {{c1::geo-replication (active geo-replication or failover groups)}}, {{c2::long-term backup retention}}, {{c3::a DNS alias on its logical server}}, or is the {{c4::SQL Data Sync sync database}}.
It still autoscales; it just stays online.
A SaaS vendor has hundreds of small tenant databases, each with low average but spiky usage at different times. How do you minimise Azure SQL cost?
Put them in an elastic pool so they share eDTUs or vCores. Pools pay off when the databases' peaks don't coincide.
How do you offload read-only reporting queries from a Business Critical Azure SQL database at no extra cost?
Use read scale-out: add ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly to the connection string to reach the built-in readable secondary. General Purpose has no such replica.
A multitenant app's write workload exceeds what a single Azure SQL database can handle. How do you scale out writes?
Shard across many databases with the elastic database tools (client library with shard map manager, plus split-merge). Scaling up has a ceiling; read scale-out helps reads only.
Azure SQL Database: what separates scaling up from scaling out?
Scale up changes one database's service objective (more vCores or DTUs, done online). Scale out spreads load across replicas or across sharded databases.
Which Azure SQL feature encrypts data files, logs and backups at rest transparently, and is on by default for new databases?
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), with a service-managed key by default. It doesn't hide data from users who can query it.
Compliance requires the company to control and be able to revoke the key protecting Azure SQL data at rest. What should you configure?
TDE with a customer-managed key: the TDE protector lives in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM, and the server identity needs get, wrapKey and unwrapKey.
Credit card columns must be unreadable even to DBAs and cloud operators, and stay encrypted inside the engine. What should you recommend?
Always Encrypted: the client driver encrypts and decrypts, and the keys never reach the database engine. TDE covers only data at rest.
Support staff must see only the last four digits of phone numbers in Azure SQL query results, with no app changes and no change to stored data. Which feature?
Dynamic Data Masking. Users with UNMASK still see the real values.
Azure SQL Dynamic Data Masking or Always Encrypted: which actually protects data from privileged users?
Always Encrypted. Masking only changes what query results show; the stored data is not encrypted.
In a multitenant Azure SQL database, each sales rep must see only the rows for their own customers, enforced in the database. Which feature?
Row-level security: an inline table-valued predicate function bound by a security policy.
Azure SQL row-level security or Dynamic Data Masking: which hides whole rows from a user?
Row-level security filters rows. Dynamic Data Masking hides values inside columns.
Azure SQL auditing can write its logs to {{c1::an Azure Storage account}}, {{c2::a Log Analytics workspace}} or {{c3::Event Hubs}}.
Azure SQL audit logs must stream to a third-party SIEM. Which auditing destination should you choose?
Event Hubs. Log Analytics suits KQL and Sentinel; Storage suits cheap long-term retention.
You need vulnerability assessment and alerts on SQL injection and anomalous access for Azure SQL. What should you enable?
Microsoft Defender for SQL in Defender for Cloud. It also covers SQL MI, SQL on VMs and Arc-enabled SQL Server.
Auditors need cryptographic proof that rows in an Azure SQL financial table were not tampered with, even by administrators. Which feature?
Ledger tables (updatable or append-only). Digests can be kept in immutable Blob storage or Azure Confidential Ledger.
A new globally distributed app stores JSON documents and needs single-digit-ms latency, elastic scale and first access to new features. Which Cosmos DB API?
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, the native API. Pick the other APIs mainly for compatibility with existing apps.

Moving existing apps to Cosmos DB with minimal code change: a MongoDB app uses {{c1::the API for MongoDB}}, a CQL app uses {{c2::the API for Apache Cassandra}}, a graph app uses {{c3::the API for Apache Gremlin}}, and an Azure Table Storage app uses {{c4::the API for Table}}.
Cosmos DB consistency levels, strongest to weakest: Strong → {{c1::Bounded staleness}} → {{c2::Session}} → {{c3::Consistent prefix}} → Eventual.
What is the default consistency level of an Azure Cosmos DB account?
Session — read-your-own-writes within a client session.
Why not simply pick the strongest Cosmos DB consistency level everywhere?
Stronger levels cost higher latency and lower availability and throughput; Strong reads also use about twice the RUs.
A shopping-cart app must always let users read their own writes while keeping latency and throughput close to eventual. Which Cosmos DB consistency level?
Session. It guarantees read-your-writes and monotonic reads per session token without Strong's cost.
Can a Cosmos DB account with multi-region writes use Strong consistency?
No. Multi-region write accounts can use every level except Strong.
A single-write-region, multi-region Cosmos DB app needs near-strong consistency with a configurable maximum lag (K versions or T seconds). Which level?
Bounded staleness. Reads lag writes by at most K versions or T time, whichever is reached first.

A good Cosmos DB partition key has {{c1::high cardinality}}, spreads {{c2::storage and request volume evenly}} so no partition runs hot, and appears in {{c3::the filter of most queries}} so they stay in one partition.
What is the storage limit of a single Cosmos DB logical partition?
20 GB. A physical partition serves at most 10,000 RU/s.
In a multitenant Cosmos DB container partitioned by TenantId, one large tenant could exceed 20 GB. What should you use?
Hierarchical partition keys (up to three levels, such as TenantId then UserId), so one tenant can span partitions.

Cosmos DB throughput: {{c1::standard (manual) provisioned}} suits steady traffic, {{c2::autoscale}} suits variable or spiky traffic, and {{c3::serverless}} suits intermittent low traffic billed per RU consumed.
A Cosmos DB workload is idle most of the day, bursts unpredictably, and must be replicated to a second region. Should you choose serverless?
No — use autoscale. A serverless account runs in a single region only.
A global app needs writes accepted in every region with low latency and 99.999% read/write availability. What should you enable in Cosmos DB?
Multi-region writes. Strong consistency is then unavailable.
How does adding regions change Cosmos DB provisioned throughput cost?
Provisioned RU/s are reserved in every region, so total throughput billed is roughly RU/s × number of regions.
An app on Azure Table Storage now needs global distribution, dedicated throughput, single-digit-ms latency and indexing of all properties. What should you recommend?
Azure Cosmos DB for Table — same Table SDKs, so minimal code change. Table Storage indexes only PartitionKey and RowKey.
Azure blob types: general files and images use {{c1::block blobs}}, append-only logging uses {{c2::append blobs}}, and VHDs with random read/write use {{c3::page blobs}}.
Blob early-deletion minimums: cool {{c1::30 days}}, cold {{c2::90 days}}, archive {{c3::180 days}}. Hot has none.
Deleting, overwriting or re-tiering earlier is charged pro rata.
Can an application read a blob directly while it is in the archive tier?
No. Archive is offline; you must rehydrate the blob to an online tier first.
Compliance data in Blob Storage must be kept 7 years, is almost never read, and a retrieval delay of hours is acceptable. Which tier minimises cost?
Archive.
Blob data is rarely read, but when it is, it must be available within milliseconds. Which tier minimises cost?
Cold (90-day minimum). Archive would need hours of rehydration.
Rehydrating a blob from the archive tier takes up to {{c1::15 hours}} at Standard priority; High priority may finish in {{c2::under 1 hour}} for blobs under 10 GB.
Blobs must move to cool after 30 days without access, to archive after 180 days, and be deleted after 7 years automatically. What should you configure?
A lifecycle management policy on the storage account.
A Spark and Hadoop analytics platform needs directory semantics, atomic directory renames and POSIX-style ACLs on object storage. What should you recommend?
Azure Data Lake Storage (Gen2): a general-purpose v2 account with hierarchical namespace enabled, so renames are fast metadata operations.
A Windows file server must move to Azure as an SMB share with AD-based NTFS permissions, keeping a local cache in branch offices. What should you recommend?
Azure Files with Azure File Sync, which turns branch Windows Servers into caches with cloud tiering.
Which media tier must an Azure Files share use to support NFS 4.1?
SSD (premium) file shares only. HDD shares are SMB only.
An SAP HANA or HPC workload needs enterprise NAS with sub-millisecond latency, very high throughput, dual-protocol NFS and SMB, and snapshots. Which Azure service?
Azure NetApp Files. Azure Files is general-purpose file shares.
Azure managed disk types, highest performance first: {{c1::Ultra Disk}} → {{c2::Premium SSD v2}} → {{c3::Premium SSD}} → {{c4::Standard SSD}} → {{c5::Standard HDD}}.
A SQL Server VM's transaction log needs sub-millisecond latency and up to hundreds of thousands of IOPS, with performance changeable without detaching the disk. Which managed disk type?
Ultra Disk — up to 400,000 IOPS per disk, adjustable at runtime. Premium SSD v2 is the cheaper option when its 80,000 IOPS suffice.

Storage account types: general blob, file, queue and table use {{c1::Standard general-purpose v2}}; high-transaction, low-latency block blobs use {{c2::Premium block blobs}}; premium SMB/NFS shares use {{c3::Premium file shares}}; premium VHDs use {{c4::Premium page blobs}}.
Azure Storage keeps {{c1::3}} copies with LRS (one datacenter) or ZRS (three zones), and {{c2::6}} copies with GRS or GZRS (three in the primary plus three LRS copies in the secondary region).
Azure Storage GRS or RA-GRS: which lets you read from the secondary region without a failover?
RA-GRS (and RA-GZRS). With plain GRS or GZRS the secondary is readable only after failover.
Blob data must survive a zone outage with no downtime and a regional outage, and the app must read from the secondary region without failing over. Which redundancy?
RA-GZRS. RA-GRS uses LRS in the primary, so a zone outage isn't absorbed without downtime.
What is the cheapest Azure Storage redundancy that keeps data available if one availability zone fails, with no geo requirement?
ZRS. LRS doesn't survive a zone loss; GRS and GZRS cost more for cross-region protection.
Users occasionally delete blobs by mistake. Which Blob Storage feature recovers deleted blobs within a retention period?
Blob soft delete.
Users occasionally overwrite blobs by mistake and need the previous content back. Which Blob Storage feature?
Blob versioning — each overwrite keeps the prior version.
After ransomware corrupts many block blobs, you want to return a whole container to its state at a past time. Which Blob Storage feature?
Point-in-time restore for block blobs. It doesn't bring back deleted containers.
Point-in-time restore for block blobs requires {{c1::blob soft delete}}, {{c2::blob versioning}} and {{c3::change feed}} to be enabled.
The restore window must be shorter than the soft-delete retention.
A regulation such as SEC 17a-4 requires blobs to be non-modifiable and non-deletable for 7 years. What should you configure?
Immutable storage (WORM) with a locked time-based retention policy, at container or version scope.
Blobs tied to pending litigation must stay unmodified until the case closes, on an unknown date. Which immutability policy?
A legal hold, which lasts until explicitly cleared. Time-based retention is for a known duration.
You need an ordered, durable log of every create, modify and delete event on blobs for auditing or downstream processing. Which feature?
Blob change feed, stored as Avro in the $blobchangefeed container.
Blob change feed or Event Grid blob events: which suits reacting to blob changes in real time?
Event Grid. Change feed is an ordered log for audit and batch processing.
Security requires storage data encrypted with keys the company controls and rotates, plus double encryption. What should you configure?
Customer-managed keys in Key Vault or Managed HSM (reached by a managed identity) plus infrastructure encryption.
VNet VMs and on-premises clients over ExpressRoute must reach a storage account on a private IP, with public access disabled. What should you use?
A private endpoint per needed sub-resource (blob, file, dfs) with a private DNS zone, then disable public network access.
Which Azure Storage SAS type does Microsoft recommend?
The user delegation SAS, because it is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials instead of the account key.
Why tie an Azure Storage service SAS to a stored access policy?
So you can revoke it by editing or deleting the policy. Otherwise an account-key SAS is revoked only by rotating the key.
A partner needs time-limited access to one container without exposing account keys, with an Entra-based audit trail. What should you issue?
A user delegation SAS scoped to the container. Revoke it by revoking user delegation keys or removing the creator's role.
You need cheap storage for petabytes of images, video and backups, accessed over HTTP/REST, with tiering. Which Azure service?
Azure Blob Storage (block blobs in general-purpose v2) with access tiers and lifecycle management. Use Azure Files only for file-share semantics.
Semi-structured IoT key/value data needs cheap, schemaless storage with lookups by key, no global distribution or secondary indexes, and cost matters most. Which Azure service?
Azure Table Storage. Cosmos DB for Table only when you need global distribution, guaranteed latency or all-property indexing.

Azure Data Factory integration runtimes: {{c1::Azure IR}} moves data between cloud stores; {{c2::self-hosted IR}} reaches on-premises or private-network data; {{c3::Azure-SSIS IR}} runs existing SSIS packages.
A nightly pipeline must copy data from an on-premises SQL Server behind a firewall to Azure Data Lake Storage. Which Azure Data Factory component is required?
A self-hosted integration runtime installed on-premises. It connects outbound over HTTPS, so no inbound ports are needed.
A company has hundreds of SSIS packages and wants to run them in Azure with minimal rework. What should you recommend?
An Azure-SSIS integration runtime in Data Factory, with SSISDB on Azure SQL Database or SQL MI.

In Azure Data Factory, a {{c1::pipeline}} groups activities, an {{c2::activity}} is one step such as Copy, a {{c3::dataset}} points at data, a {{c4::linked service}} holds connection info, and a {{c5::trigger}} starts a run.
What is OneLake in Microsoft Fabric?
A single, tenant-wide logical data lake for all Fabric items, storing tables in open Delta Parquet format on ADLS Gen2 technology.
Fabric users need to query data already in ADLS Gen2 and Amazon S3 without copying it into OneLake. What should you use?
OneLake shortcuts.
An Azure SQL operational database must be replicated into OneLake in near real time for analytics. Which Fabric feature?
Mirroring.
Fabric Lakehouse or Warehouse: which suits a SQL-skilled team needing full T-SQL DDL/DML and multi-table transactions?
Warehouse. A Lakehouse is engineered mainly with Spark; both store Delta tables in OneLake.
A company wants one SaaS analytics platform covering ingestion, engineering, warehousing, real-time analytics and Power BI, with unified storage and capacity-based billing. What should you recommend?
Microsoft Fabric, with all workloads on OneLake.
Azure Synapse dedicated or serverless SQL pool: which bills per TB of data processed?
Serverless SQL pool, which queries lake files ad hoc. A dedicated pool is a provisioned MPP warehouse sized in DWUs.
Analysts occasionally need T-SQL over Parquet files in ADLS Gen2, without provisioning infrastructure or loading data. What is the cheapest option?
Synapse serverless SQL pool. In Fabric, a Lakehouse shortcut with its SQL analytics endpoint does the same.
Data scientists and engineers need a collaborative Apache Spark platform for large-scale engineering and machine learning on Delta Lake, with Unity Catalog governance. Which service?
Azure Databricks.
IoT telemetry from Event Hubs must be analysed in real time with SQL-like queries over tumbling and sliding windows to raise alerts, with no cluster to manage. Which service?
Azure Stream Analytics. Data Factory is batch orchestration, not real-time processing.
Every event through an event hub must be archived automatically to Blob or ADLS for later batch processing, with no code. What should you enable?
Event Hubs Capture, which writes files on a time or size window, whichever comes first.
Engineers need interactive, ad-hoc analysis of huge volumes of log and telemetry time-series data with fast KQL queries. Which service?
Azure Data Explorer (in Fabric: an Eventhouse in Real-Time Intelligence). Not for OLTP.
Business users need interactive dashboards and reports over warehouse or lakehouse data, shared across the organisation. What should you recommend?
Power BI.
Medallion architecture: {{c1::bronze}} holds raw data as ingested, {{c2::silver}} holds cleansed and conformed data, {{c3::gold}} holds curated, business-ready aggregates.

Pick the Azure service: scheduled batch ETL/ELT orchestration → {{c1::Azure Data Factory}}; real-time stream processing in SQL → {{c2::Azure Stream Analytics}}; big-data Spark and ML → {{c3::Azure Databricks}}; log and telemetry exploration in KQL → {{c4::Azure Data Explorer}}.
An existing Azure PaaS design needs a large T-SQL data warehouse with MPP performance and compute you can pause when idle. Which option?
Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool. For a new design, Microsoft points to Fabric Warehouse.
RPO vs RTO for an Azure workload: which one limits data loss and which limits downtime?
RPO caps data loss, measured as time back to the last recoverable point. RTO caps downtime until the service is running again.
An Azure workload may lose at most 15 minutes of data in a disaster. Is that an RPO or an RTO requirement?
RPO — it decides how often you must back up or replicate. RTO would instead drive the recovery method (restore vs failover).
Azure Backup or Azure Site Recovery: which one protects against accidental deletion and ransomware with long retention?
Azure Backup — point-in-time copies kept from days to years. Site Recovery replicates for fast failover, not history.
Azure Backup or Azure Site Recovery: which one fails whole VMs over to another region within minutes?
Azure Site Recovery — continuous replication plus orchestrated failover, with an RPO of minutes instead of the hours you get from Backup.
Why is Azure Site Recovery not a substitute for Azure Backup?
It replicates every change, including deletions, corruption and ransomware encryption, and keeps no long-term point-in-time history.
Recovery Services vault or Backup vault: which one protects Azure Blobs and Azure managed disks?
Backup vault — it also covers Azure Database for PostgreSQL and AKS. Choosing a Recovery Services vault here is the classic distractor.
Recovery Services vault or Backup vault: which one protects Azure VMs, SQL Server in Azure VMs and Azure Files?
Recovery Services vault — it also receives MARS agent, MABS and DPM backups.
Azure VM backups must be restorable in the paired region during a regional outage, and DR drills must run there. Which vault settings do you need?
A Recovery Services vault on GRS with Cross Region Restore turned on. CRR isn't available on LRS or ZRS vaults.
Backup data must not leave the region but must survive a datacenter (zone) failure. Which Azure Backup vault redundancy do you choose?
ZRS — copies across availability zones in the same region. GRS would send a copy to the paired region.
Azure Backup vault redundancy: {{c1::LRS}} for cheap dev/test data, {{c2::ZRS}} to survive a zone failure in-region, {{c3::GRS}} to survive a regional outage and allow Cross Region Restore.
Azure Backup soft delete: how long is deleted backup data kept?
14 days by default, adjustable from 14 to 180 days. Deleted backup data can be undeleted during that window.
Why set Azure Backup enhanced soft delete to always-on?
An attacker can't switch it off and then purge the backups; once always-on, soft delete can't be disabled.
Compliance requires that nobody, not even a subscription Owner, can delete Azure Backup recovery points or shorten retention early. What do you configure?
An immutable vault with immutability locked. Locking is irreversible; unlocked immutability can still be turned off.
Why doesn't Azure Backup soft delete alone stop an admin from destroying backups early?
The admin can still reduce retention or wait out the soft-delete window. Only locked immutability blocks shortening retention.
How do you stop a single rogue Azure Backup admin from disabling soft delete or deleting backup data?
Turn on multi-user authorization (MUA) with a Resource Guard placed in another subscription or tenant that a security admin controls.
MARS agent or MABS: which one backs up Windows files, folders and system state to Azure without an extra server?
The MARS agent — installed directly on the Windows machine, sending to a Recovery Services vault.
On-premises SQL Server, Exchange and Hyper-V VMs need application-aware backup to Azure. MARS agent or MABS/DPM?
MABS (or System Center DPM) — an on-premises backup server that keeps a local disk copy and sends a copy to Azure. MARS isn't app-aware.
Azure VM backup: Standard or Enhanced policy for several backups per day?
Enhanced — every 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours. Standard takes one backup a day.
Azure VMs use Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks. Which Azure VM backup policy type must you use?
The Enhanced policy — the Standard policy can't protect those disk types.
An Azure VM needs a backup RPO of 4 hours. What do you configure?
An Azure Backup Enhanced policy on an hourly schedule every 4 hours. An RPO of minutes needs Site Recovery instead.
Azure VM backup: why does restoring from Instant Restore snapshots give a lower RTO than restoring from the vault tier?
The snapshots sit next to the VM's disks, so nothing has to be copied back from the vault before the restore.
How does Azure Backup take an application-consistent backup of a Windows Azure VM?
Through VSS (Volume Shadow Copy Service), via the backup extension, which flushes application data to disk before the snapshot.
Azure Backup of a Linux VM is only file-system consistent. What makes it application-consistent?
Pre- and post-scripts that quiesce the application around the snapshot.

Azure VM backup consistency: {{c1::application-consistent}} means the app restarts with no data loss; {{c2::file-system consistent}} means files are consistent but the app may need its own recovery; {{c3::crash-consistent}} is like pulling the power plug.
A company needs Azure VMs to fail over to another Azure region with an RPO measured in minutes and minimal manual steps. What do you recommend?
Azure Site Recovery (Azure-to-Azure). It replicates continuously and creates crash-consistent recovery points every 5 minutes.
Why is Azure Backup with Cross Region Restore a poor fit for a regional DR RPO of minutes?
Its secondary-region RPO is in hours (up to 36) and restoring from the vault is slow; Site Recovery gives minutes.
Azure Site Recovery: crash-consistent or app-consistent recovery points, which one also captures in-memory data and in-flight transactions?
App-consistent (VSS on Windows). Crash-consistent captures only what is on disk.
Azure Site Recovery creates crash-consistent recovery points every {{c1::5 minutes}} (fixed) and app-consistent points at most every {{c2::1 hour}}.
Site Recovery protects a SQL Server VM and a print server. Which one needs app-consistent recovery points?
The SQL Server VM — a database needs in-memory and in-flight data captured. Crash-consistent is enough for print, file or DHCP servers.

Azure Site Recovery for on-premises VMware VMs or physical servers needs an on-premises {{c1::replication appliance}}, the {{c2::Mobility service}} agent on each protected machine, and a {{c3::Recovery Services vault}} in Azure.
The modernized replication appliance replaces the old configuration server and process server. Physical servers use the same architecture.
Azure Site Recovery for Hyper-V VMs: which components go on the Hyper-V hosts?
The Site Recovery Provider and the Recovery Services agent on each Hyper-V host (the Provider goes on the VMM server if VMM manages the hosts). Nothing inside the VMs.
A multi-tier app (web, app, SQL) must fail over in a set order, with a script to update DNS between steps. Which Site Recovery feature do you use?
A recovery plan: ordered groups of machines, with manual actions and Azure Automation runbooks between the groups.
Azure Site Recovery: what makes several VMs of one app share the same consistent recovery points?
Multi-VM consistency — put the VMs in one replication group.
How do you validate an Azure Site Recovery DR plan without affecting production replication?
Run a test failover into an isolated VNet, check the app, then run Cleanup test failover. Replication keeps running throughout.
Why shouldn't an Azure Site Recovery test failover use the production VNet?
Duplicate IP addresses and hostnames would clash with the production VMs, which are still running.
Azure SQL Database automated backups: full backups {{c1::weekly}}, differential backups every {{c2::12 or 24 hours}}, transaction log backups about every {{c3::10 minutes}}.
This schedule is what makes point-in-time restore possible. Hyperscale uses storage snapshots instead.
Azure SQL Database point-in-time restore: what retention range can you configure?
1 to 35 days, default 7. The Basic tier is limited to 1–7 days.
Azure SQL Database point-in-time restore: where does the restored database land?
A new database on the same logical server; PITR doesn't overwrite the existing database.
A regulation requires keeping monthly Azure SQL Database backups for 7 years. What do you configure?
A long-term retention (LTR) policy with a monthly rule. LTR keeps full backups for up to 10 years; PITR stops at 35 days.
Azure SQL Database geo-restore: which backup storage redundancy does it need?
Geo-redundant (GRS) or geo-zone-redundant (GZRS) backup storage; geo-restore rebuilds the database in any region from those replicated backups.
Why is geo-restore the cheapest but slowest regional DR option for Azure SQL Database?
It needs no standby replica, but you rebuild from backups that lag behind, so RPO and RTO run from minutes to hours.
Data-residency rules say Azure SQL Database backups must not leave the region. Which backup storage redundancy do you choose?
Zone-redundant (ZRS) or locally redundant backup storage; ZRS also survives a zone failure. The default GRS copies backups to the paired region.
Azure SQL Database backup storage is set to LRS or ZRS. Which recovery option do you lose?
Geo-restore — it needs geo-replicated (GRS or GZRS) backups.
How should you back up SQL Server running in an Azure VM with central management and an RPO of about 15 minutes?
Azure Backup for SQL Server in Azure VM to a Recovery Services vault: full, differential and log backups, with logs as often as every 15 minutes.
Why isn't a plain Azure VM backup enough for SQL Server point-in-time recovery?
It only snapshots the whole VM, at most every 4 hours and with no log backups, so you can't restore to a moment between snapshots.
Azure Cosmos DB periodic or continuous backup: which one lets you restore an accidentally deleted container to a specific second yourself?
Continuous backup — self-service point-in-time restore. Periodic backup restores need a support request.
Which Azure Cosmos DB continuous backup tier has no backup storage charge?
The 7-day tier. The 30- and 35-day tiers bill backup storage per GB per region; restores are charged in every tier.
Azure Blob backup: operational or vaulted, which one survives deletion of the source storage account?
Vaulted backup — copies go to a Backup vault and can be kept up to 10 years. Operational backup lives inside the source account.
A team needs fast recovery from accidental blob changes without copying data out of the storage account. Which Azure Blob backup type fits?
Operational backup — continuous local protection built on blob PITR; it also places a delete lock on the account.
Azure Blob point-in-time restore: which features must you enable first?
Blob soft delete, change feed and blob versioning. PITR works on block blobs in general-purpose v2 accounts.
A whole blob container was deleted. Can Azure Blob point-in-time restore bring it back?
No — use container soft delete. PITR only restores blobs inside containers that still exist.

Azure Storage self-service recovery: {{c1::blob versioning}} recovers a blob after an overwrite, {{c2::blob soft delete}} recovers deleted blobs or snapshots, and {{c3::container soft delete}} recovers deleted containers.
Blob data must be kept unmodifiable (WORM) for legal reasons. Which Azure Storage feature do you use?
Immutable storage — a time-based retention policy or a legal hold.
What does Azure blob object replication do?
It asynchronously copies block blobs from a source container to a destination container in another storage account, in a region you choose.
Why isn't Azure blob object replication a backup on its own?
It replicates deletions and corruption too, so a bad change reaches the destination as well.
Blob object replication or GRS: which one lets you pick the destination region?
Object replication; GRS always replicates to the paired region.
Azure Files backup: snapshot tier or vault-standard tier, which one survives loss of the storage account?
Vault-standard — data is copied offsite into the Recovery Services vault. Snapshot-tier share snapshots live in the same account.
Branch offices use Windows file servers synced with Azure File Sync. What is the simplest way to back up the data?
Back up the Azure file share (the cloud endpoint) with Azure Backup, not each server. The cloud endpoint holds the full dataset even when servers tier files.
Which Azure service backs up individual managed disks without backing up the whole VM?
Azure Disk Backup in a Backup vault — agentless incremental snapshots, several times a day if needed.
Azure Disk Backup or Azure VM backup: which one gives app-consistent backups of the whole VM?
Azure VM backup in a Recovery Services vault. Disk Backup is crash-consistent and per disk.
Which Azure service backs up AKS cluster state and persistent volumes?
Azure Backup for AKS: a Backup extension in the cluster writes to a Backup vault, with snapshot and vault tiers for Azure Disk volumes.
Which Azure portal experience centrally manages Azure Backup and Site Recovery across vaults, subscriptions and regions?
Resiliency in Azure, formerly Azure Business Continuity Center (which replaced Backup center).
Every Azure VM with a given tag must get backup configured automatically. What do you use?
A built-in Azure Policy that configures Azure Backup on VMs carrying that tag.
Azure availability set: fault domain or update domain, which one protects against hardware failure?
Fault domain — VMs sharing power and a network switch. Update domains group VMs that reboot together during planned maintenance.
An Azure availability set has up to {{c1::3}} fault domains and up to {{c2::20}} update domains (default {{c3::5}}).

Azure VM connectivity SLA: a single VM with Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2 or Ultra on all disks gets {{c1::99.9%}}; two or more VMs in an availability set get {{c2::99.95%}}; two or more VMs across availability zones get {{c3::99.99%}}.
A VM-based tier in Azure needs at least 99.99% availability. How do you deploy it?
Two or more VMs across availability zones; an availability set tops out at 99.95%.
An app tier on Azure VMs must survive the loss of an entire datacenter in the region. Availability set or availability zones?
Availability zones — VMs or a scale set across 2–3 zones behind a zone-redundant Standard Load Balancer or Application Gateway v2. Availability sets stay inside one datacenter.
Do Azure availability zones protect a workload against a full region outage?
No — they cover zone failures only; a region outage needs a second region.
VM Scale Sets: Flexible or Uniform orchestration, which one works with Azure Backup and Site Recovery?
Flexible — standard VMs that can mix sizes and Spot. Uniform runs identical instances through scale-set APIs, for large stateless fleets.
What does Microsoft recommend instead of availability sets for new Azure VM deployments?
VM Scale Sets with Flexible orchestration, which spread VMs across zones or fault domains.

A zone-redundant App Service plan needs a {{c1::Premium v2, v3 or v4}} plan (or Isolated v2 in ASE v3), a region with availability zones, at least {{c2::2}} instances, and zone redundancy enabled on the {{c3::plan}}.
Basic and Standard plans can't be zone-redundant. The feature itself is free, but you pay for the minimum instances.
A web app on Azure App Service must survive a full region outage. What do you add?
A second deployment in another region behind Front Door or Traffic Manager; zone redundancy covers only zone failures.
AKS: how do you make a cluster highly available within one region?
Spread node pools across availability zones and use the Standard or Premium tier for a financially backed API server SLA.
AKS clusters in two regions must both pull images if one region fails. What do you use for the images?
Azure Container Registry Premium with geo-replication, with the clusters behind Front Door or Traffic Manager.
Azure SQL Database General Purpose or Business Critical: which one fails over faster because replicas hold the data on local SSD?
Business Critical — a primary plus up to 3 synchronous replicas. General Purpose starts a new stateless node and reattaches remote storage, with a cold cache.
Azure SQL Database: which service tiers can't use zone redundancy?
DTU Basic and Standard. vCore General Purpose, Business Critical and Hyperscale, and DTU Premium, all support it.
Azure SQL Database: active geo-replication or failover group, which one keeps the same connection endpoint after failover?
Failover group — its read-write and read-only listeners follow the primary. With active geo-replication the server name changes.
Azure SQL Database: active geo-replication or failover group, which one fails over a set of databases together?
Failover group; active geo-replication fails over each database separately.
Azure SQL Database: which geo-DR option offers an optional Microsoft-managed automatic failover policy?
Failover groups; active geo-replication fails over only when you trigger it.
Why can a forced geo-failover in Azure SQL Database lose data?
Geo-replication is asynchronous, so transactions not yet sent to the secondary are lost.
An app connects to five Azure SQL databases and must reach the DR region after failover without changing connection strings. What do you recommend?
A failover group. The app connects to the read-write listener <fog-name>.database.windows.net, which DNS repoints to the new primary.
Azure SQL failover group: customer-managed or Microsoft-managed failover policy, which one does Microsoft recommend?
Customer-managed — you trigger failover from your own monitoring. Microsoft-managed waits for a region-wide outage plus the grace period, so it may come late.
How do you provide cross-region DR for Azure SQL Managed Instance?
A failover group between two managed instances in different regions. It replicates all user databases and provides read-write and read-only listeners.
SQL Server on Azure VMs: Always On availability group or failover cluster instance, which one gives readable secondaries with separate storage per replica?
Availability group — database-level protection, with optional async replicas in another region. An FCI shares storage and has no readable secondaries.
SQL Server on Azure VMs: when does a failover cluster instance fit better than an availability group?
When instance-level objects must fail over together, such as SQL Agent jobs and logins, because an FCI protects the whole instance.

Azure Cosmos DB availability SLA: single region {{c1::99.99%}}, single region with availability zones {{c2::99.995%}}, multiple regions with multi-region writes {{c3::99.999%}} for both reads and writes.
An Azure Cosmos DB account has one write region and several read regions. What read and write availability SLA does it get?
99.999% for reads; writes stay at 99.99%.
An Azure Cosmos DB app needs five-nines write availability. What do you enable?
Multi-region writes (active-active); a single write region caps writes at 99.99%.
An Azure Cosmos DB account has one write region and several read regions. How do you make writes resume automatically if the write region fails?
Enable service-managed failover and set the region failover priority; Cosmos DB then promotes the next region to write region.

Azure Storage redundancy: {{c1::LRS}} keeps 3 copies in one datacenter; {{c2::ZRS}} spreads 3 copies across availability zones; {{c3::GRS}} adds an LRS copy in the paired region; {{c4::GZRS}} is ZRS plus an LRS copy in the paired region.
An app must keep reading blob data during a primary-region outage without waiting for failover, and also survive a zone failure in the primary. Which redundancy do you choose?
RA-GZRS. GZRS allows no secondary reads before failover; RA-GRS does, but uses only LRS in the primary region.
Azure Storage customer-managed failover: planned or unplanned, which one avoids data loss and keeps geo-redundancy?
Planned failover — used while both regions are healthy, for drills or migration. It syncs first, then swaps the roles.
Before an unplanned Azure Storage failover, what tells you how much data you may lose?
The Last Sync Time — writes after it may not have reached the secondary, because geo-replication is asynchronous.
Front Door or Traffic Manager for multi-region failover of an HTTPS web app?
Front Door — a global layer-7 anycast proxy, so failover isn't delayed by DNS caching; it adds WAF and caching too.
A non-HTTP (TCP) app needs global failover across Azure regions. Front Door or Traffic Manager?
Traffic Manager — DNS-based, so it works for any protocol, though failover waits on DNS TTL. The cross-region Load Balancer is the layer-4 alternative.
Which Traffic Manager or Front Door routing method gives active-passive failover?
Priority routing.
How do you calculate the composite SLA of Azure services chained in series, where all must be up?
Multiply the SLAs: SLA₁ × SLA₂ × … The result is always lower than the weakest component.
Composite SLA: a web app on App Service (99.95%) uses Azure SQL Database (99.99%). What is the composite SLA?
0.9995 × 0.9999 ≈ 99.94%, about 26 minutes of allowed downtime a month.
Composite SLA: the same 99.94% deployment runs active-active in two Azure regions. Ignoring the global router, what is the combined availability?
How do you calculate the availability of N redundant Azure deployments running in parallel?
1 − (1 − A)^N: subtract from 1 the chance that all of them are down at once.
Why does Front Door (99.99%) end up limiting a two-region active-active design that is otherwise at 99.99996%?
The router sits in series with both regions: 0.9999996 × 0.9999 ≈ 99.99%.
Composite SLA: 2 VMs in an availability set (99.95%) behind a Standard Load Balancer (99.99%) write to a storage account (99.9%). What is the composite SLA?
0.9995 × 0.9999 × 0.999 ≈ 99.84%. The storage account is the weakest link.
An Azure SQL Database needs the highest single-region availability SLA and must survive a zone failure with no data loss. What do you deploy?
Business Critical (or DTU Premium) with zone redundancy: 99.995% SLA and RPO 0. A failover group adds regional DR but doesn't raise the in-region SLA.
Azure SQL Database needs an RTO under 1 minute for a regional disaster, and reporting must run on the DR copy. What do you choose over geo-restore?
A failover group with a readable geo-secondary; point reporting at the read-only listener. Geo-restore takes minutes to hours and has no readable copy.
Azure Cosmos DB multi-region writes or a single write region: which one supports strong consistency?
Single write region. Multi-region writes rule out strong consistency and need conflict handling, in exchange for 99.999% writes and local write latency.
Azure Cosmos DB multi-region writes: what is the default conflict resolution policy?
Last writer wins, by timestamp; a custom stored-procedure policy is the alternative.
A legacy app needs full OS control, custom drivers and a specific Windows Server version. Which Azure compute should you recommend?
Azure Virtual Machines (IaaS), in a VM Scale Set if it must scale out. PaaS options such as App Service or Container Apps give no OS or driver access.

Azure compute decision tree: full OS control → {{c1::Virtual Machines}}; managed web apps and APIs → {{c2::App Service}}; short event-driven code → {{c3::Azure Functions}}; low-code integration workflows → {{c4::Logic Apps}}.

Azure compute decision tree for containers and batch: serverless microservices without running Kubernetes → {{c1::Container Apps}}; full Kubernetes API control → {{c2::AKS}}; one container fast, no orchestration → {{c3::Container Instances}}; large-scale parallel HPC jobs → {{c4::Azure Batch}}.
Azure VM families: general purpose = {{c1::D}}-series; burstable = {{c2::B}}-series; compute-optimized = {{c3::F}}-series; memory-optimized = {{c4::E}}-series.

Azure VM families: storage-optimized with high local disk throughput = {{c1::L}}-series; GPU = {{c2::N}}-series; HPC with InfiniBand = {{c3::H}}-series; largest memory for SAP HANA = {{c4::M}}-series.
A low-traffic dev/test web server idles most of the day with short CPU spikes. Which Azure VM series fits most cheaply?
B-series (burstable): it banks CPU credits while idle and spends them during bursts.
A regulated company needs its VMs on physical servers not shared with any other Azure customer, and wants control over host maintenance timing. What should you recommend?
Azure Dedicated Host: whole physical servers reserved for your subscription, grouped in host groups, with maintenance controlled through maintenance configurations.
Azure Dedicated Host or an isolated VM size: which gives you host-level control over maintenance and placement?
Dedicated Host. An isolated VM size also fills a whole physical server, but you get no control over the host itself.
A nightly rendering job is interruptible, restarts from checkpoints, and must be as cheap as possible. Which Azure VM purchase option should you use?
Azure Spot VMs, in a scale set or Batch pool: deep discounts on spare capacity, but they can be evicted at any time and have no SLA.
When Azure evicts a Spot VM, what does the Deallocate eviction policy keep that Delete does not?
The disks: the VM stops and you keep paying for its storage, so it can restart later. Delete removes the VM and its disks.
Azure Reservations or a savings plan for compute: which fits workloads that change VM size or region, or move to App Service?
Savings plan: an hourly spend commitment applied across sizes, regions and eligible compute services. Reservations discount more but lock to one size and region.
Which Azure benefit cuts VM cost by reusing existing Windows Server or SQL Server licences, on top of a reservation?
Azure Hybrid Benefit: it removes the licence part of the price and stacks with reservations or savings plans.
A web tier on VMs must add instances when CPU is high, shrink at night, and spread across availability zones. What should you use?
Virtual Machine Scale Sets spanning zones, with metric-based and schedule-based autoscale rules, behind a Standard Load Balancer or Application Gateway.
VM Scale Sets or availability sets: which one can autoscale?
Scale Sets. Availability sets only spread a fixed set of VMs across fault and update domains in one datacenter.
A company must give 2,000 call-center workers Windows desktops from Azure, with many users sharing each session host to cut cost. What should you recommend?
Azure Virtual Desktop with a pooled host pool on Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session.
Azure Virtual Desktop pooled or personal host pool: which gives each user their own persistent VM?
Personal. In a pooled host pool users share session hosts and land on any available one.
In Azure Virtual Desktop, where should user profiles live so users get the same profile on any pooled session host?
FSLogix profile containers on an SMB share: usually Azure Files Premium, or Azure NetApp Files for very large, high-IOPS deployments.
AKS or Azure Container Apps: a team wants microservices with scale to zero and Dapr, without managing clusters or needing the Kubernetes API. Which?
Azure Container Apps: serverless containers with KEDA scaling and Dapr built in. Choose AKS when you need the Kubernetes API, custom operators or node pool control.
A team runs a containerized script for 10 minutes once a day, with no orchestration, paying only per second while it runs. What should you recommend?
Azure Container Instances (or a Container Apps job): per-second billing with no cluster. AKS would keep nodes running all day.
A team has one containerized web API and wants managed TLS, custom domains, deployment slots and built-in auth with minimal container know-how. Which service?
App Service (Web App for Containers). For many event-driven microservices use Container Apps; for full Kubernetes, AKS.
AKS clusters in three regions pull the same images and need low-latency regional pulls, one registry name, and private endpoints. Which Azure Container Registry tier?
Premium, with geo-replication: geo-replication and private endpoints are Premium-only features.
